title: Rav Chinena
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Bekhorot 32a we find “Rav Chinena said that Rav said,” and in Nedarim 28a “Rav Chinena said that Rav Kahana said that Shmuel said.” And what we find in Berakhot 33a, “Rabbi Acha the Tall taught before Rav Chinena,” Hyman proposes there “before Rav Huna,” as in Dikdukei Soferim. In Tamid 31b: “Rav Chinena in the name of Rabbi Assi, and Rabbi Assi in the name of Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Yitzchak.” Hyman suggests that he is Rabbi Chanina of Tzippori, Rabbi Mani’s colleague, and Rabbi Assi is the one called in the Jerusalem Talmud Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Yonah’s colleague.

notes.text: The supplied כתמיד is read as Tamid. Saved Davidson Tamid 31b actually contains the full Chinena/Assi/Shmuel-bar-Rav-Yitzchak chain, resolving a potential nonlocation concern. Hyman’s Palestinian identity conjectures remain conjectures, not an external identity verdict.

Tamid 31b directly preserves the Chinena–Assi–Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak chain. The exact Dikdukei Soferim reading and Hyman’s proposed Palestinian identities have not been independently established here.
